newsitem.title: USA: Fergie says U.S. gives her a second chance.
newsitem.headline: Fergie says U.S. gives her a second chance.

text.p: Disgraced British royal Sarah Ferguson turned up on David Letterman's "Late Night" television show on Monday and told a cheering audience she loved America because "you give me a second chance over here."

Wearing a two-piece black Chanel suit, the Duchess of York continued to blame the British press for being cruel to her. "I've caught a bit of flak, you know what I mean," she told the host as the audience exploded in wild applause.
The duchess, known familiarly as "Fergie," said she likes the United States because "people are nice" to her.

"You really do cheer me up. I guess you give me a second chance," she said. "I can walk down the street without people saying she's fat, she's thin, her skirts are too short, too long, too this, too that. Freebie Fergie does it again."

Ferguson, divorced last May from Prince Andrew, Queen Elizabeth's second son, said on the Letterman show she still has a friendly relationship with her former husband and he had called her before her appearance on the television programme to wish her well.

She is in the United States touting her new 306-page book called "My Story" which was published last Wednesday. In the just-published autobiography, Ferguson blames herself, loneliness, a history of self-hatred, betrayals by friends and the British press for her estrangement from the Royal Family.
As for other members of the Royal Family, she said: "I don't think they'll be opening the front door and getting the champagne out.
"I certainly think I'd like to retain a good relationship with Her Majesty as grandmother to my two girls," she added.
She attributed most of her troubles to "growing up (and) I matured very late and I think I matured on a public stage," she said.

When Letterman asked how her two daughters felt about being a princess, the audience vigorously applauded when Ferguson replied: "They understand that every little girl is a princess and every little girl has the right to be special."
